title: Unpatched Danfoss AK-SM800A Flaws Allow Takeover
content_md: Six unpatched vulnerabilities in the Danfoss AK-SM800A, a system manager that runs refrigeration in supermarkets and cold storage sites, could let a remote attacker take over the controller without logging in. The flaws became public on November 11, 2026, and there is still no fixed firmware version and no CVE ID for any of them. The timing raises the stakes. Since October 11, 2026, attackers have tampered with internet-exposed refrigeration controllers across Europe. Germany’s Federal Office for Information Security (BSI), the Centre for Cybersecurity Belgium (CCB) and Ireland’s NCSC now tell operators to take AK-SM800A management interfaces off the internet, with a VPN as the minimum for any remote connection. BSI rates the issue criticality 3 (Orange), its level for immediate action, and the CCB confirmed the findings on November 12. What Did Researchers Find Inside the AK-SM800A Firmware? Carlo Meijer of Dutch security firm Midnight Blue spotted the bugs within about an hour, using firmware from the Danfoss website.
